label: Synthetic training data
summary: Synthetic training data refers to text or other content generated by AI itself and used to train future AI models. It emerges as a proposed response to the scarcity of high-quality human-produced data, particularly books. The concern is that this creates a feedback loop where AI is essentially training on its own output.
how_maaike_uses: Maaike treats synthetic training data as a symptom of a deeper problem: the mismatch between what machine learning requires and what humans actually value. She is sceptical of the idea that AI-generated novels could substitute for human writing, not just on technical grounds but on humanistic ones. Her core worry is about removing the human from the loop entirely, particularly when we do not yet know how ambient and integrated these systems will become. She also points out the uncomfortable irony that we might industrialise the very thing writers struggle to earn a living from, reducing books to cheap fodder for machines.
open_questions: What exactly makes books better training data than other text sources, and could synthetic data ever replicate those qualities?
If AI cannot generate anything genuinely new, can it produce the kind of original, stylistically varied writing that makes books useful for training in the first place?
What does it mean for collective human knowledge if the most important datasets are increasingly populated without any human having read or evaluated the content?
